title: RoseTTAFold All-Atom designs proteins that bind small molecules
summary: RoseTTAFold All-Atom extends deep-learning structure prediction from proteins alone to full assemblies with nucleic acids, small molecules, metals and covalent modifications. Its diffusion version, RFdiffusion All-Atom, built proteins around target small molecules, and designs binding digoxigenin, heme and bilin were confirmed by crystallography and binding measurements. Dated to the bioRxiv preprint of 9 October 2023, which already reports these validated designs; the peer-reviewed paper appeared in Science (issue of 19 April 2024). Success rates and affinities were not read for this entry.
organization: University of Washington Institute for Protein Design

evidence.tested: Designed binders for digoxigenin, heme and bilin were experimentally validated by crystallography and binding measurements; prediction accuracy was benchmarked against AlphaFold2 and on CAMEO small-molecule docking.
evidence.unknown: The abstracts give no design success rates, numbers of designs tested or binding affinities; these figures were not read for this entry.
evidence.ai_role: RoseTTAFold All-Atom, a deep network trained on PDB assemblies, models proteins with nucleic acids, small molecules, metals and covalent modifications; RFdiffusion All-Atom, fine-tuned from it on denoising, generated the small-molecule-binding protein designs.

source_review.scope: bioRxiv v1 metadata and abstract, Europe PMC and PubMed metadata and abstract of the Science paper, IPD announcement of 30 October 2023.
